elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3.2.1 requires CGL of "[***] dollars ($[***]) per occurrence"; the limit is redacted, so no USD 1,000,000 floor can be verified, and the redline does not add one.

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Section 12.3.2.1 states "[***] dollars ($[***]) Product and Completed Operations aggregate"; the aggregate figure is redacted and is limited to Product/Completed Operations, so the USD 2,000,000 general aggregate cannot be confirmed. No redline addresses it.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence sets SFJ E&O at "one million dollars ($1,000,000)", below the preferred USD 2,000,000; Section 12.3.2.4 imposes professional liability only on subcontractors at a redacted limit.

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence sets cyber and privacy liability at "two million dollars ($2,000,000)", below the preferred USD 5,000,000 trigger amount.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: No workers' compensation item appears in the cited 12.3.2.1–12.3.2.4 list or in the inserted language; a workers' compensation subsection may exist elsewhere in Section 12.3 but is not in the record, and the redline expressly declines to press it.

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: The rationale asserts Section 12.3.1 already provides certificates on request, but that provision is not in the cited or rendered operative language, so it cannot be verified here.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "SFJ will maintain professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance with a minimum limit of one million dollars ($1,000,000)" — imposed directly on SFJ rather than only on subcontractors as in 12.3.2.4.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "cyber and privacy liability insurance with a minimum limit of two million dollars ($2,000,000)" — the Agreement previously contained no cyber/privacy cover at all.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted sentence directly obligates the counterparty (SFJ) to carry E&O at USD 1,000,000 and cyber/privacy at USD 2,000,000, curing both defects (E&O previously imposed only on subcontractors at a redacted limit; no cyber cover anywhere).

Preferred level is not reached: E&O is USD 1,000,000 (not 2,000,000), cyber is USD 2,000,000 (not 5,000,000), the CGL per-occurrence and aggregate figures remain redacted and unverifiable, and workers' compensation and certificates-on-request are not confirmed in the operative text. This is acceptable as a deliberate fallback landing, and the comment correctly says so.

Minimal: nothing is deleted, the mutual insurance programme (CGL, umbrella, clinical trials liability, subcontractor professional liability, additional-insured/product liability) is retained intact, and the drafter correctly omitted the model language's non-required extras (at-own-expense, one-year survival tail, certificate mechanic), adding only the two fallback coverages and burdening only the counterparty rather than expanding the mutual obligation.

Preserves intent: allocation, duration (the 12.3.2 chapeau's "during the Term" and greater-of-Applicable-Law floor), cost-sharing and country-specific mechanics in 12.3.2.3 survive without contradiction; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created.

Drafting clean-up (not a defect in substance): the insertion is rendered as an unnumbered heading appended after 12.3.2.4 — number it "12.3.2.5" so it slots cleanly into the 12.3.2 list, and consider a short lead-in (e.g., "Notwithstanding the reference to each Party in Section 12.3.2, SFJ will maintain...") so the SFJ-only obligation reads consistently with the chapeau's "each Party will maintain the following types of insurance coverage."
If the counterparty pushes back on cyber cover, the fallback is already the ask; there is no lower position short of walk-away for a party processing Customer Data.
